lore.title: Corva and Gall
lore.body:
**Corva** is a red dwarf at the dead end of a minor lane. Its one prize is **Gall**, a gas giant whose upper atmosphere is rich in deuterium and helium-three. Gall has eleven moons; only **Kettle**, a cracked ice shell over a black ocean, has ever held people.

The lane mouth, the **Throat**, opens near Gall's trailing Trojan point, so ships come out of the dark almost on top of the giant.

Gall's colours: ochre bands, bruise-purple storms, a white cap at the south pole. Dippers call its weather by the colour of the bruise.

lore.title: The Lamp
lore.body:
Catalogued as **Ide's Comet** (first recorded 2128), called **the Lamp** by everyone who has ever lived under it. Its orbit is resonant with Gall: every two hundred and sixty-odd years it falls in from the dark, passes close by the giant at perihelion, and goes back out past the cold for two and a half centuries.

Recorded perihelia: 2128, 2391, 2654, 2917.

At aphelion the Lamp's ice is under thirty kelvin. It is one of the coldest places a person could reach and still come back from — if they had the fuel to come back.

lore.title: The Throat and the lanes
lore.body: Lanes are tunnels in the way space is folded, opening at points of balance near large masses. A lane is held open at each end by an **anchor**; without its anchor a lane goes raw — tidal, unpredictable — and over decades it closes. Lanes also heal, very slowly, if nothing collapses them again.

lore.title: Dipping
lore.body:
A skimmer like the **Patience** holds a high orbit over Gall and lets down a forty-kilometre carbon tether. On the end is the **Bucket**, a heat-shielded scoop that rides through the cloud-tops at orbital speed, swallowing gas. A dip lasts six hours; the line sings the whole time.

The **tether-chief** runs the drum, the reel-out, the tension and the release. **Runners** ride crawlers out along the line to clear ice and fix sensors. **Riggers** maintain the Bucket and the drum.

The **Sling** is a tether-chief's trick: spin the line with a craft on the end and let go at the exact moment, and you can throw something a very long way.

Dippers give their dead to Gall: the body is lowered on the line and released into the Deep.

lore.title: Bonded labour and the air-tithe
lore.body: A Halloran-Vey worker is **bonded**: their passage, food, suits and air are charged against them, and the debt passes to their children. The air-tithe is the line on the ledger that never goes away. A worker can be moved, sold or *relocated* with their debt; the debt is the Combine's property.

lore.title: The Halloran-Vey Combine
lore.body: An extraction company of the twenty-fourth century: deuterium, ice, ore, people. It ran Corva for sixty years through a resident factor, a skimmer, a supply ship and a camp of two thousand families on Kettle. Its legal successor is the **Concord of Vey**.

lore.title: Tamsin's Rock
lore.body: A Combine mining station in another system. When its bonded struck in 2379, the factor used a Sanitation Agent. Four thousand people died in their bunks in one night shift; the machines never stopped. Within a year the Combine had resettled the station with new bonded and it was turning a profit.

lore.title: Sanitation Agents
lore.body: Combine designation for an engineered aerosol agent that attacks human neural tissue and nothing else. Victims go quiet and sleep within hours; hence the bonded name, **the Hush**. Supplied in a sealed ceramic egg kept below forty kelvin in a cryo-sleeve. The shell is fail-deadly: breached, or warmed past forty kelvin, it vents. The agent survives vacuum as dormant spores. It is destroyed only by sustained extreme pressure and heat together.

lore.title: The Purchase
lore.body:
As taught in the shared schools of Patience: *In 2391 the Three Hundred of the Patience bought the ship and the Corva claim from the Halloran-Vey Combine for one share, and set it on Kettle. We bought our air.*

Every shared child can recite the catechism. The **Blank Share** — the scratched first line of the Share Plate — is said to be the Company's share, struck off when the Purchase was complete.

lore.title: The Spine
lore.body: The hull of the old skimmer stands upright in Kettle's ice, the spine of the city. Its drum hall is the Council nave; its cargo decks are the Archive; its old docks still open on a shaft to the surface. The Share Plate hangs in the nave.

lore.title: Shared and unshared
lore.body: A **Share** is a hereditary right in the city: a vote, a seat in the nave, and air without tithe. About twelve thousand people hold one. The other hundred and seventy thousand — descendants of the Camp, of later settlers, of refugees from three wars — are **unshared**. They pay the air-tithe, measured and collected by **air-wardens**.

lore.title: The Lampers
lore.body: A heresy of the lower warrens, tolerated because it is poor. Lampers keep Lampfast when the Lamp is in the sky, and say that the city's comfort was bought with something the founders sent away: *The Lamp comes round, the debt comes due.*

lore.title: The Concord of Vey
lore.body: A corporate-feudal power three lanes from Corva, built out of the bankrupt Halloran-Vey Combine and a dozen others. It holds its worlds by title, its crews by debt, and its fleets by the very old custom of paying the officers first.

lore.title: Cinderhaven
lore.body: Ring-station of the Tarn Reach. Docks, debt-houses, repossession yards, chapels. Everything on Cinderhaven is owed to somebody, and the debt-houses keep their ledgers in stone vaults because the Directorate's courts burn so often.

lore.title: The Roundsmen
lore.body: A faith carried out of Corva by dippers who left before its lane went dark. *What goes out comes back. Nothing is lost, only on its way.* Roundsmen keep a calendar of returns and say that the Lamp takes the dead out and brings them back.

lore.title: The Lamp Hoard
lore.body: A dock legend of the Tarn Reach: that the founders of Corva hid their wealth on their comet, and that it comes back every time the Lamp does. Salvagers have been drinking to it for two hundred years. Nobody has been through the Corva lane in all that time to check.
